title: 14-day rotation — Sunday batch

background.schedule: Sunday batch prep; 5–10-minute meals on other days; Wednesday shakes; weekend restaurant breakfasts

tuna.title: Spicy tuna–avocado rice
ingredients: 2 cans light tuna, 170 g each before draining
1 tsp soy sauce; 1 tbsp lime; optional sriracha
steps: Reheat the MON lunch rice for 2–3 min until hot.
Drain both tuna cans; dice ½ avocado and ½ cucumber.
Mix tuna, soy and lime; serve on rice with fresh vegetables.
tuna.before: Rice was batch-cooked Sunday. Canned tuna and fresh ingredients are opened only now.

gingerbeef.title: Ginger–soy beef, soba and broccoli
ingredients: 225 g lean ground beef, RAW before Sunday's cooking
ONE tied Blue Dragon soba bundle (~83 g DRY; do not cook the whole 250 g package)
2 tbsp (30 mL) water for the sauce
steps: MONDAY — remove the completely cooked beef–soba–broccoli container from the fridge. No extra sauce or seasoning is needed: everything was added Sunday.
Microwave covered for about 3–5 min, stirring halfway, until the centre reaches 74°C / 165°F. Eat immediately.
gingerbeef.before: Sunday prep: cook the meat, soba and broccoli; mix and add the soy–honey–sesame–ginger sauce in the skillet BEFORE packing. Monday: just reheat.
gingerbeef.tip: Exactly ONE of the three tied Blue Dragon soba bundles (~83 g dry), never the entire 250 g packet. The soy, honey, sesame oil and ginger go into one sauce bowl and are poured over cooked beef before mixing in noodles and broccoli.
batch_steps: SUNDAY — SAUCE FIRST: in a small bowl, mix 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp honey, 1 tsp sesame oil, ½ tsp ginger and 2 tbsp water. Set aside. Do not pour the sauce into the pasta cooking water.
SOBA: bring water to a boil in a saucepan. Add ONE Blue Dragon tied bundle (about 83 g DRY) only, cook as directed on its packet, then drain.
BROCCOLI: put 1½ cups frozen broccoli in a covered microwave-safe bowl with a splash of water. Microwave about 4–6 min until hot and tender; drain excess water.
BEEF: heat a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat; add 225 g RAW lean ground beef. Break it apart with a spatula and brown for about 6–8 min, until fully cooked (71°C / 160°F).

SAUCE GOES ON THE BEEF: reduce heat to medium and pour the entire bowl of soy–honey–sesame–ginger sauce into the skillet with the cooked beef. Stir and simmer 1–2 min until it lightly coats the meat (do not boil it dry).
COMBINE: add drained cooked soba and cooked drained broccoli to the sauced beef. Toss gently over medium heat about 1 min until evenly coated.
PORTION: transfer the entire dish to the labelled MON dinner shallow container. Cool promptly and refrigerate within 2 hours.

lemonpotato.title: Lemon chicken and potatoes
ingredients: 200 g REGULAR potatoes weighed RAW, AIR-FRIED Sunday
½ cup tomatoes; ½ cup cucumber
1 tsp olive oil; 1 tsp Dijon; 1 tbsp lemon; ¼ tsp oregano
steps: Reheat the TUE lunch chicken and potatoes 3–5 min to 74°C / 165°F.
Dice tomatoes and cucumber.
Mix oil, Dijon, lemon and oregano; pour over hot chicken and fresh vegetables.
lemonpotato.before: Both chicken and potatoes were completely cooked Sunday.

chili.title: Turkey chili over rice
ingredients: 1 of 3 cooked chili portions made Sunday using 600 g RAW ground turkey total
Batch chili includes 796 mL crushed tomatoes, one 540 mL can black beans, bell pepper, onion, chili spices
steps: Reheat labelled TUE dinner chili and rice covered 4–6 min, stirring halfway, to 74°C / 165°F.
Serve chili over rice.
chili.before: Sunday batch makes THREE equal chili portions: Tue, Fri and one frozen spare.
chili.tip: No stove or fresh cutting today.

fajitas.title: Chicken fajita rice bowl
ingredients: 1 sliced bell pepper + ½ onion COOKED Sunday with fajita spices
¾ cup canned black beans; 1 tbsp salsa; 1 tsp lime
steps: Thaw THU chicken/pepper/rice in fridge WED night.
Add drained beans; microwave covered 4–6 min until 74°C / 165°F.
Top with salsa and lime.
fajitas.before: ONE portion, not the old two-serving recipe. Cooked and FROZEN Sunday.
fajitas.tip: Thu food must not stay refrigerated from Sunday.

salmon.title: Maple–Dijon salmon, potatoes and green beans
ingredients: 225 g RAW salmon BAKED in oven Sunday with 1 tbsp Dijon + 2 tsp maple syrup
200 g REGULAR potatoes weighed RAW, AIR-FRIED in Ninja Sunday with 2 tsp olive oil
steps: Thaw the THU salmon and potatoes in fridge WED night.
Microwave frozen green beans with 2 tbsp water covered 4–6 min.
Gently heat cooked salmon and potatoes covered to 74°C / 165°F; add lemon.
salmon.before: Salmon baked IN OVEN Sunday; potatoes cooked IN NINJA Sunday.
salmon.tip: Texture of reheated salmon is softer than fresh baked.

meatballs.title: Batch-cooked marinara penne and Angus meatballs
ingredients: 150 g fully cooked frozen Compliments Angus meatballs (NOT Long Phung)
¾ cup marinara + 2 cups baby spinach + 1 tsp dried basil, combined Sunday
steps: Thaw FRI lunch penne–meatball container in fridge THU night.
Microwave covered 4–6 min, stir halfway, until 74°C / 165°F.
meatballs.before: Pasta and meatballs both preheated and fully assembled Sunday.

chilipotato.title: Loaded turkey chili potatoes
ingredients: 1 of 3 equal turkey chili portions COOKED Sunday
250 g REGULAR potatoes weighed RAW, AIR-FRIED Sunday
steps: Thaw FRI dinner chili/potatoes in fridge THU night.
Microwave covered 4–6 min until 74°C / 165°F, stirring chili halfway.
Serve chili over potatoes.
chilipotato.before: Chili and potatoes COOKED Sunday; no baking Friday.
chilipotato.tip: Third chili portion is a freezer spare, NOT a Week 2 dependency.

porkchop.title: Garlic–lime pork and sweet potato
ingredients: 225 g RAW boneless pork BAKED Sunday
250 g sweet potato weighed RAW, AIR-FRIED Sunday
1 tsp olive oil + 1 tbsp lime juice; garlic and paprika used Sunday
steps: Thaw SAT pork/sweet potato in fridge FRI night.
Microwave frozen green beans with 2 tbsp water covered 4–5 min.
Heat cooked pork and sweet potato to 74°C / 165°F and add lime.
porkchop.before: Pork and sweet potato fully cooked Sunday, then FROZEN.
porkchop.tip: Initially cook pork chop to 71°C / 160°F; reheat leftovers to 74°C / 165°F.

thaicurry.title: Thai coconut shrimp curry and rice
ingredients: 250 g RAW peeled shrimp COOKED Sunday
1 cup light coconut milk + 2 cups frozen Asian vegetables + 1 tbsp red curry paste, COOKED Sunday
steps: Thaw SUN curry/rice in fridge SAT night.
Microwave covered 4–6 min, stir halfway, until 74°C / 165°F; add lime.
thaicurry.before: Cooked during the PREVIOUS Sunday's batch and frozen.
thaicurry.tip: 250 g shrimp, not the entire 340 g bag.

tunabeans.title: Tuna, white bean and potato bowl
ingredients: 200 g REGULAR potatoes weighed RAW, AIR-FRIED Sunday
1 cup cherry tomatoes; 2 tsp olive oil; 1 tbsp lemon
steps: Reheat the cooked MON potatoes for 2–3 min.
Drain tuna and beans; halve cherry tomatoes.
Mix all with olive oil and lemon.
tunabeans.before: Potatoes COOKED Sunday. Tuna and beans canned until Monday.
tunabeans.tip: 200 g refers to RAW potato weight.

oregano.title: Lemon–oregano chicken rice bowl
ingredients: ¾ cup tomatoes; ¾ cup cucumber
2 tsp olive oil; 1 tbsp lemon; ½ tsp oregano; garlic used Sunday
steps: Reheat MON chicken and rice covered 3–5 min to 74°C / 165°F.
Dice tomatoes and cucumber; add lemon and olive oil.
Serve with hot chicken/rice.
oregano.before: All chicken and rice cooked Sunday. Rice from total 2⅔ standard cups (~480 g) DRY for Week 2.
oregano.tip: 225 g chicken means RAW weight before cooking.

peanutnoodle.title: Peanut chicken rice bowl
ingredients: 1½ tbsp peanut butter; 1 tbsp soy; 1 tbsp lime; 2 tbsp hot water
steps: Reheat TUE chicken, rice and frozen vegetables covered 4–6 min to 74°C / 165°F.
Mix peanut butter, soy, lime and hot water; stir into hot bowl.
peanutnoodle.before: Uses rice instead of dry rice noodles: no weekday noodle boiling.

tacoskillet.title: Smoky taco beef rice bowl
ingredients: 225 g RAW-equivalent ground beef COOKED with taco spices Sunday
¾ cup canned black beans; ½ cup FROZEN corn
steps: Reheat TUE taco beef/rice with drained beans and frozen corn, covered 4–6 min to 74°C / 165°F.
Add salsa and optional avocado.
tacoskillet.before: Sunday cooks both beef and rice.
tacoskillet.tip: No raw beef or pepper cutting Tuesday.

shrimpmango.title: Lime–chili shrimp, mango and rice
ingredients: 250 g RAW peeled shrimp COOKED Sunday
½ cup FROZEN mango chunks thawed; ½ cucumber
1 tbsp lime; 1 tsp olive oil; optional chili flakes
steps: Thaw THU shrimp/rice and frozen mango in fridge WED night.
Reheat shrimp/rice covered 3–5 min until 74°C / 165°F.
Dice cucumber and add mango and lime to the hot bowl.
shrimpmango.before: Cooked shrimp and rice FROZEN Sunday; mango used cold.

harissa.title: Harissa chicken, chickpeas and vegetables
ingredients: 225 g RAW-equivalent chicken COOKED with 1 tbsp harissa + 2 tsp olive oil Sunday
steps: Thaw THU harissa chicken in fridge WED night.
Add drained chickpeas and frozen vegetables; microwave covered 4–6 min to 74°C / 165°F.
Add lemon if desired.
harissa.tip: Chickpeas are already cooked in the can.

chickenpotato.title: Sweet-chili chicken loaded potatoes
ingredients: 250 g REGULAR potatoes weighed RAW, AIR-FRIED Sunday
½ cup FROZEN corn; 1 cup bagged shredded cabbage
1 tbsp sweet chili sauce or salsa
steps: Thaw FRI chicken and potatoes in fridge THU night.
Add frozen corn and reheat covered 4–6 min to 74°C / 165°F.
Top with pre-shredded cabbage and sweet chili sauce.
chickenpotato.tip: 250 g potatoes means RAW weight before cooking.

koreanbeef.title: Sticky Korean-style ground beef rice
ingredients: 225 g RAW-equivalent ground beef COOKED Sunday with 1 tbsp soy, 1 tsp maple, 1 tsp sesame oil
steps: Thaw FRI beef/rice in fridge THU night.
Add frozen broccoli; microwave covered 4–6 min, stir halfway, to 74°C / 165°F.
koreanbeef.before: Ground beef used instead of strips for easier Sunday batching.
koreanbeef.tip: Sauce is already on the precooked beef.

tomatocurry.title: Tomato–coconut chicken curry and rice
ingredients: ¾ cup crushed tomatoes + ½ cup light coconut milk + 2 cups baby spinach
1 tsp curry powder + ½ tsp garam masala, curry cooked Sunday
steps: Thaw SAT chicken curry/rice in fridge FRI night.
Reheat covered 4–6 min, stirring halfway, until 74°C / 165°F.
tomatocurry.before: Entire curry cooked and frozen Sunday.

stickypork.title: Sticky sesame pork with ready-to-use udon
ingredients: 225 g RAW pork strips COOKED Sunday with 1 tbsp soy + 1 tbsp sweet chili + 1 tsp sesame oil
ONE 200 g pack READY-TO-USE plain udon (NOT dry soba)
steps: Thaw SUN cooked pork in fridge SAT night.
Combine pork, 200 g ready-to-use udon, frozen vegetables and 2 tbsp water; microwave covered 5–7 min, stirring halfway, to 74°C / 165°F.
stickypork.before: Pork COOKED the PREVIOUS Sunday; udon package must say READY-TO-USE.
stickypork.tip: If noodles require boiling, follow label instead; total time may exceed 10 min.

restaurant.title: Your regular restaurant breakfast
steps: This is your regular Saturday/Sunday breakfast AT A RESTAURANT. No home cooking or grocery shopping is required for this meal.
Order 2 eggs, 2 sausages, 2 slices rye bread and your usual portion of breakfast potatoes.
For planning only, the 850–1,100 kcal estimate is approximate; serving sizes and cooking methods vary by restaurant.
restaurant.tip: Restaurant meal: do not add any of these ingredients to the home grocery order.
restaurant.before: Restaurant meal. No home cooking or grocery purchase required.

shakechoc.title: Chocolate–banana shake (make 3)
ingredients: PER SHAKE (make three separately during the day): 1½ scoops whey, preferably chocolate
1 tsp (5 mL) unsweetened cocoa (optional with chocolate whey)
steps: These quantities make ONE shake. Repeat three times on Wednesday; full-day amount is 4½ scoops whey, 90 g oats, 3 tbsp peanut butter and 1½ bananas.
Blend 300 mL cold water and 30 g dry rolled oats for 15–20 seconds to break up the oats.
Add 1½ scoops whey, 1 tbsp peanut butter, ½ banana, optional 1 tsp cocoa and optional ice.
Blend with lid closed 30–45 seconds until smooth. If too thick, add 50 mL water and blend 10 seconds more.
Drink now, then prepare the other shakes separately later, to reach three total. Don't leave a mixed shake at room temperature for hours.
shakechoc.tip: Vanilla whey works too: use 1 tsp cocoa for a chocolate taste. Actual macros depend on scoop weight and whey brand.
shakechoc.before: Each ingredient amount is for ONE shake. Repeat THREE times on Wednesday.

shakeberry.title: Vanilla–berry shake (make 3)
ingredients: PER SHAKE (make three separately): 1½ scoops whey, preferably vanilla
100 g frozen mixed berries (straight from freezer)
steps: These quantities make ONE shake. Repeat three times on Wednesday; full-day amount is 4½ scoops whey, 90 g oats, 3 tbsp peanut butter and 300 g frozen berries.
Blend 300 mL cold water and 30 g dry oats for 15–20 seconds.
Add 1½ scoops whey, 1 tbsp peanut butter, 100 g still-frozen berries and optional ¼ tsp cinnamon. Add ice if desired.
Blend with lid closed for 45–60 seconds. If large fruit pieces remain, stop the blender, stir with a spoon, then blend another 15 seconds.
If too thick, add 50 mL water and blend 10 more seconds. Drink promptly; make the remaining shakes as needed.
shakeberry.tip: Use peanut butter, not almond butter; no extra purchase is needed. Berries go in frozen; cinnamon is optional.
shakeberry.before: Each ingredient amount is for ONE shake. Repeat THREE times on Wednesday.

notes: V3: all hot proteins and rice are cooked Sunday; weekdays reheat/assemble in 5–10 min after overnight fridge thawing.
Sunday takes about 40–60 min hands-on and 75–120 min overall including cooking and packing.
Meat and potato weights are RAW, before Sunday cooking. DRY rice quantities are in the batch guide.
Do not keep Thu–Sun cooked meals refrigerated since Sunday: freeze them Sunday and thaw in fridge overnight.
Cool rapidly in shallow containers, refrigerate/freeze within two hours. Reheat leftovers once to 74°C / 165°F.
Calories/macros are estimates; adjust for labels and portions.
No cheese or sour cream; Wednesday shakes and weekend restaurant breakfast remain.

batch_prep.title: Sunday prep — Week 1
batch_prep.intro: Batch once before Week 1. The two weeks can be started in either order. Freeze every Thu–Sun cooked portion on prep day.
batch_prep.equipment: Oven, Ninja dual-basket air fryer, rice cooker, large pot, skillet, shallow labelled meal containers.
steps: LABEL containers first: MON tuna/rice, MON beef/soba, TUE lemon chicken/potato, TUE chili/rice, THU fajita chicken/rice, THU salmon/potato, FRI penne/meatballs, FRI chili/potato, SAT pork/sweet potato, SUN shrimp curry/rice. Add one extra chili container marked SPARE.

RICE COOKER: measure exactly 1⅔ STANDARD measuring cups (~300 g) of DRY rice. Add water per rice package and cook (not 1⅔ rice-cooker scoops). After cooking, divide approximately 5 cups: MON tuna 1½; TUE chili 1; THU fajitas 1; SUN shrimp curry 1½.

NINJA: cut 650 g REGULAR raw potatoes into 2–2.5 cm cubes. AIR FRY at 200°C for 22–25 min with about 5 tsp olive oil total, shake halfway. Divide by INITIAL RAW weight: TUE 200 g, THU 200 g, FRI 250 g. Other basket: 250 g raw diced sweet potato + 1 tsp oil, AIR FRY 200°C for ~18–23 min. Optional soaking adds 20 min; dry very well.

OVEN 200°C / 400°F: cook 450 g RAW chicken until 74°C / 165°F, about 20–25 min; split evenly into TWO cooked portions equivalent to 225 g raw each. On separate trays cook 225 g salmon with 1 tbsp Dijon + 2 tsp maple (about 12–18 min, until 70°C / 158°F) and 225 g boneless pork to 71°C / 160°F. Timing depends on thickness; pull each tray when ready.
FAJITA VEGETABLES: cook 1 sliced pepper + ½ onion with smoked paprika and cumin on an oven tray or in skillet; pack with THU chicken. TUE chicken stays plain; add lemon-Dijon dressing when serving.

CHILI: brown 600 g RAW lean ground turkey in large pot to 74°C / 165°F; add 1 can 796 mL crushed tomatoes, 1 can 540 mL black beans (rinsed), 1 diced bell pepper, ½ diced onion, 2 tsp chili powder, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika. Simmer about 20 min. Divide FINISHED chili evenly into 3 containers: TUE dinner, FRI dinner, spare freezer portion. Optional slow cooker after browning: HIGH ~3–4 h (longer elapsed time).

BEEF/SOBA: in a bowl mix SAUCE = 1 tbsp soy + 1 tsp honey + 1 tsp sesame oil + ½ tsp grated ginger + 2 tbsp water. Boil ONE tied Blue Dragon soba bundle (~83 g DRY) per package (NOT all 250 g); drain. Microwave 1½ cups frozen broccoli covered with a little water 4–6 min until hot; drain. Brown 225 g RAW lean ground beef in a skillet ~6–8 min to 71°C / 160°F. REDUCE to medium heat and POUR THE SAUCE INTO THE COOKED BEEF; stir 1–2 min. Add drained soba and cooked broccoli; toss 1 min. Pack MON dinner and refrigerate promptly.
PENNE/MEATBALLS: boil 90 g DRY penne. Heat 150 g fully cooked frozen Angus meatballs in ¾ cup marinara with 2 cups baby spinach and 1 tsp basil. Combine, pack FRI lunch.

SHRIMP CURRY: simmer 1 cup light coconut milk + 1 tbsp red curry paste + 2 cups FROZEN Asian vegetables. Add 250 g thawed RAW peeled shrimp; cook to 74°C / 165°F. Pack SUN curry beside its measured 1½ cups cooked rice.

COOL / STORE: refrigerate MON and TUE meals promptly; freeze all THU–SUN labelled portions and chili spare on Sunday. Keep fresh vegetables/cans unopened until serving. Move a frozen portion into the refrigerator the EVENING BEFORE its day.
portions: RICE: 5 cups cooked = 1½ MON tuna + 1 TUE chili + 1 THU fajitas + 1½ SUN curry.
CHICKEN: 450 g raw = 2 portions (TUE lemon, THU fajitas), each equivalent to 225 g raw.
TURKEY CHILI: 600 g raw turkey yields 3 equal cooked servings (TUE, FRI, spare).
POTATOES: 650 g raw = 200 TUE + 200 THU + 250 FRI; SWEET POTATO 250 g SAT.
OTHER: beef 225 g + ONE soba bundle MON; salmon 225 g THU; meatballs 150 g + penne 90 g FRI; pork 225 g SAT; shrimp 250 g SUN.
storage: MON/TUE cooked meals at or below 4°C in fridge; later meals at -18°C in freezer until the day before.
Chill rice and cooked proteins rapidly in shallow containers and refrigerate/freeze within two hours.
Use refrigerated leftovers within 2–3 days; reheat leftovers only once to 74°C / 165°F throughout (stir halfway).
If thawing takes longer, use fridge earlier; do not leave food on the counter. Day-of fresh cucumber/avocado/tomatoes are not frozen.

batch_prep.title: Sunday prep — Week 2
batch_prep.intro: Week 2 is INDEPENDENT of Week 1: no chili leftovers are required. Everything hot is cooked here, not on weekday evenings.
batch_prep.equipment: Oven, Ninja dual-basket air fryer, rice cooker, skillet, shallow labelled meal containers.
steps: LABEL MON tuna/potato; MON lemon chicken/rice; TUE peanut chicken/rice; TUE taco beef/rice; THU shrimp/rice; THU harissa chicken; FRI sweet-chili chicken/potato; FRI Korean beef/rice; SAT tomato–coconut chicken/rice; SUN sesame pork. Mark THU–SUN FREEZE.

RICE COOKER: measure exactly 2⅔ STANDARD cups (~480 g) DRY rice, add package-recommended water, cook. Yield ~8 cups COOKED. Measure: MON chicken 1½; TUE peanut chicken 1; TUE taco beef 1; THU shrimp 1½; FRI Korean beef 1½; SAT curry 1½.
NINJA: dice 450 g REGULAR RAW potatoes. Toss with ~3 tsp olive oil. AIR FRY 200°C 22–25 min, shake halfway. Portion MON 200 g and FRI 250 g by initial RAW weight.

OVEN 200°C / 400°F: roast 1,150 g RAW chicken to 74°C / 165°F (~20–30 min depending on thickness), then split into 5 labelled cooked portions corresponding to RAW weights: MON 225 g oregano, TUE 225 g peanut, THU 225 g harissa, FRI 225 g sweet-chili potato, SAT 250 g curry. Roast 225 g pork strips separately to 71°C / 160°F.

BEEF: brown 450 g RAW lean ground beef to 71°C / 160°F. Split into TWO equal cooked portions: TUE tacos (½ tsp chili powder, ¼ tsp cumin, ¼ tsp smoked paprika), FRI Korean (1 tbsp soy, 1 tsp maple, 1 tsp sesame oil).
SHRIMP: cook 250 g RAW peeled, thawed shrimp until 74°C / 165°F; pack and freeze for THU mango rice bowl. Frozen mango is thawed overnight before serving, NOT cooked with shrimp.

CHICKEN FLAVOURS: add oregano/garlic to MON chicken, leave TUE peanut chicken plain (1-minute sauce Tuesday), coat THU chicken with 1 tbsp harissa and 2 tsp olive oil, leave FRI potato chicken plain (sweet chili added at serving).

SAT CURRY: simmer ¾ cup crushed tomatoes + ½ cup light coconut milk + 2 cups baby spinach + 1 tsp curry powder + ½ tsp garam masala. Add the SAT cooked chicken portion (250 g RAW-equivalent); cool and freeze with its rice.
SUN PORK: add 1 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp sweet chili and 1 tsp sesame oil to the cooked pork. Keep ONE 200 g READY-TO-USE udon packet unopened and 2 cups frozen Asian vegetables frozen for Sunday.

COOL / STORE: refrigerate MON/TUE meals, freeze THU–SUN cooked portions on prep day. Move frozen food into fridge the night before. Cans of tuna/beans, fresh produce, bagged cabbage, and udon stay in their proper packaging until use.
portions: RICE: 8 cups cooked = 1½ MON oregano + 1 TUE peanut + 1 TUE tacos + 1½ THU shrimp + 1½ FRI beef + 1½ SAT curry.
CHICKEN: 1,150 g raw = four 225 g portions (Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri) plus one 250 g portion (Sat).
BEEF: 450 g raw = two portions of 225 g (Tue taco, Fri Korean). PORK: 225 g raw for Sun. SHRIMP: 250 g raw for Thu.
POTATOES: 450 g raw = 200 MON tuna + 250 FRI chicken. UDON: ONE ready-to-use 200 g packet SUN.
FRESH/READY FOOD: tuna/white beans MON; mango + cucumber THU; shredded cabbage FRI.
storage: MON/TUE refrigerated at 4°C or lower; THU–SUN frozen Sunday at -18°C.
Transfer frozen portions to fridge the evening before the day; never thaw cooked meals on counter.
Cool rice/proteins quickly in shallow containers; refrigerate or freeze within two hours. Reheat leftovers once to 74°C / 165°F.
Total time is 75–105 min Sunday, but serving-day microwave/assembly tasks are designed for 5–8 min.
